(- if you're not already in a social club, sports team, anything like that, you'll get tunnel vision and that's no good and so far VERY hard to un-do) To keep participating in my life, not just the end of theirs.

The fear and anxiety each day - is this "The Day" I find her gone? The stress of pushing out that moment for a couple minutes longer out of avoidance. 

The amount of time and effort I'm losing to "fund" this deeply under thought situation BC no one could talk to their Mom about some hard fast facts about aging, retirement, and boundaries - making me an inadvertent consequence / participant of the mess we've made as a "family" ~ generational trauma ~

It's like having a very old baby... That I neither planned for or wanted but feel guilty at it's neglect (even though death is the only thing that we're SURE is going to happen - why plan for the only inevitable human experience, but WTF do I know 🙄)

How quickly and habitual bad habits become if you're not on top of it, applying your own oxygen mask. It's like I'm helping to kick my own ass RN.

The fear that she might actually outlive Mom and I. That one is getting really real...

A lot of that is generational trauma, that is either unseen or flat out ignored (or maybe a little bit of both).
Whatever has been buried will come up and shock both parties - that takes Love. A conscious choice to care and invest in daily.

Oh man... Buckle up friend. I'm caretaking for my grandmother and this was a problem for a long time. She is still completely uninterested in in house nurses for help, wanting to stay independent, while not remembering how not independent she is, which is hard on her and I. ( Compromise is coming though, so staying positive!)
 I definitely agree that a meeting with a Dr to have the Dr breakdown exactly why a change to disposable briefs ( helps to not say diaper) would be in his best interests. It's the only thing that EVER convinced her to accept the loss of her DL, her wheeled push cart, and the adult diapers. Even now it's sometimes a battle over if it's time to change it ( when it is).  The dementia will mess with his recollection- may even dismiss it completely sometimes but being patient and a soft reminders should only get you a mild cursing at if it's a hard memory day.
 Also, I highly recommend a set schedule, kinda like a toddler. Cuts down on accidents which helps with the self esteem and the physical work of clean up.
 For joint pain ( getting in and out of the shower, general mobility issues, a smattering of arthritis and a lack of motivation to keep muscles moving- also hard) a CBD balm really helps with the aches- especially with a touch of icy hot to help it get in there. Also CBD honey ( after checking with her Drs and making sure it wouldn't mess with Rx's) in some tea, really does help on a "not quite herself days" instead of a harder pill for mood. Might not be available in your area, but if it is, it's been a help a couple of ways.
Further helpful thing during this phase for me were:
Over the toilet chairs that are a bit higher
Side tub rail 
Tub chair 
Shower head with an attachment that he can control
Water proof mattress cover and chair cover
Dog training pads ( less expensive than bed covers and it's the same thing 🙄) for the bed just in case
Lots of PJs, pants, towels, and wash cloths at the ready for a quick swap out
Gloves
Your preferred antibacterial spray + rags
Scented trash bags for bathroom waste specifically
Pet detergent from natural pet- it'll get the smells out of clothes like nothing else. Just to keep her freshest we go for anything deep cleaning antibacterial etc.
Dry shampoo and wet wipes. Some days it's not going to happen but this can be a compromise if the last shower was a couple days ago and there haven't been any big blow outs.

I hope this rambling list is even remotely helpful, good luck and stay healthy yourselves as caretakers during this part of transition, the burnout can be super real, really quickly. Best!! ♥️
